name: chunks
algorithm: Each standard library's chunk iterators over n splitmix64 u64 values: per round r a piece length k = (r % 16) * 4 + 1; a mut pass scales every element of piece j to x * 3 + j, then a shared pass adds, per piece, its first element xor its last and every element; the rounds' sums are added with wrapping (README.md).

skip.c: no chunk iterator in C's standard library
skip.zig: no mut chunk iterator in Zig's standard library (std.mem.window hands out const pieces only); a hand-sliced mut pass would be a stand-in, which the idiomatic table refuses
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum folds every element of every piece of both passes, so every column visited the same pieces in the same order
notes: Iterators: Mk Slice.ChunksMut (raw pointer and count) and Slice.Chunks (a position into the borrowed slice) over a HeapList[u64]; Rust slice::chunks_mut and slice::chunks; Go slices.Chunk (Go 1.23) for both, its pieces aliasing the slice; Zig has no column: its std has no mut chunk iterator.

The mut pass's inner loop is each language's element iterator over the piece (Mk for e in mut c, Rust iter_mut); Go writes c[i] in a range over the piece's indices, whose bounds checks its compiler removes; the shared pass reads c[0] and c[c.Len() - 1] and then iterates.
